questions.stem: Minor salivary glands:

options.label: A
options.text: lie in the submucosa and open by short ducts

options.label: B
options.text: are compound glands with long main ducts

options.label: C
options.text: are found only in the lips and cheeks

options.label: D
options.text: secrete only under strong nervous stimulation

options.label: E
options.text: are absent from the palate and tongue

questions.why: Named by site: buccal, labial, lingual, palatine.

questions.stem: The vestibule communicates with the oral cavity proper when the teeth are clenched through the:
questions.why: The gap behind the last molars.

questions.stem: The mucosa of the hard palate differs from that of the cheek because it is:

options.label: A
options.text: keratinised and firmly bound to bone

questions.why: Masticatory mucosa resists friction during chewing.

questions.stem: The most common type of keratinisation in the gingiva is:
questions.why: The surface squames keep pyknotic nuclei.

questions.stem: The muscular core of the lip is the:
questions.why: Skeletal muscle encircling the mouth.

notes.E: Upper lip elevator, not the core.

questions.stem: The vermilion zone of the lip needs moistening by saliva because it:

options.label: A
options.text: has no salivary or sweat glands

options.label: D
options.text: has many sebaceous glands that dry it

questions.why: It has very thin keratin and a rich capillary bed.

questions.stem: The tongue is described as musculoglandular because it is made of:

options.label: A
options.text: skeletal muscle with glands between fibres

options.label: C
options.text: skeletal muscle covered by glandular skin

questions.why: Muscle bundles run in three planes, with glands among them.

questions.stem: The foramen caecum of the tongue marks the:

options.label: D
options.text: end of the circumvallate papillae row

questions.why: At the apex of the V-shaped sulcus terminalis.

notes.D: They lie in front of the sulcus.

questions.stem: Which papillae give the dorsum of the tongue its rough texture and have no taste buds?
questions.why: Most numerous, highly keratinised, mechanical role.

questions.stem: Von Ebner's glands are associated with the:
questions.why: Their serous secretion flushes the furrow and provides lingual lipase.

questions.stem: Which taste bud cells act as stem cells?
questions.why: They lie at the base of the bud.

questions.stem: The hardest tissue of the body, made mostly of hydroxyapatite, is:
questions.why: About 96–98% mineral, made by ameloblasts.

questions.stem: Dentin can be repaired throughout life because:
questions.why: Their processes run in dentinal tubules.

questions.stem: Cementocytes most closely resemble:
questions.why: Cementum is bone-like but avascular.

questions.stem: Serous acinar cells can be recognised by their:

options.label: B
options.text: flat nuclei pressed to the base

questions.why: Round basal nuclei with rough ER below and granules above.

questions.stem: Myoepithelial cells in salivary glands function to:

options.label: A
options.text: squeeze secretion out of the acini

options.label: E
options.text: form the capsule of the gland

questions.why: They lie between the secretory cells and the basal lamina.

questions.stem: Intercalated ducts are best developed in the:
questions.why: They are long and numerous in serous glands.

questions.stem: A gland with purely serous acini, numerous intercalated ducts and fat cells in the stroma is the:
questions.why: Fat increases with age; the facial nerve runs through it.

notes.E: Serous, but not a salivary gland.

questions.stem: Most of the unstimulated (resting) saliva comes from the:
questions.why: About 60–70%; the parotid gives most stimulated saliva.

questions.stem: A ranula is a mucous retention cyst most often arising from the:
questions.why: Bluish swelling in the floor of the mouth.

questions.stem: The palatine tonsil lies between the:

options.label: B
options.text: soft palate and posterior pharyngeal wall

questions.why: In the tonsillar fossa of the oropharynx.

questions.stem: The oral cavity proper is continuous behind with the oropharynx through the:
questions.why: The retromolar gap links vestibule and oral cavity proper.

questions.stem: The depressed midline area between the nose and the vermilion border of the upper lip is the:
questions.why: Answer: A.

questions.stem: The lower lip is separated from the chin by the:
questions.why: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which layer of the oral mucous membrane is NOT always present?
questions.why: Absent, e.g., under the ventral tongue and midline of the hard palate.

questions.stem: Lining mucosa covers all of these EXCEPT the:
questions.why: The hard palate has masticatory mucosa.

questions.stem: Specialised mucosa is found on the:

options.label: A
options.text: dorsum and sides of the tongue

options.label: D
options.text: floor of the mouth and gums

questions.why: It contains papillae and taste buds.

notes.D: Floor is lining; gums are masticatory.

questions.stem: Parakeratinisation of the skin epidermis may be seen in:
questions.why: In the mouth it is normal, mostly in the gingiva.

questions.stem: In orthokeratinised epithelium, the surface squames:

options.label: A
options.text: stain bright pink and lack nuclei

questions.why: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Filiform papillae are arranged in rows that run:

options.label: B
options.text: at right angles to the midline

questions.why: Their tips point backward.

questions.stem: Fungiform papillae look red in young children because their epithelium is:

options.label: D
options.text: full of capillaries in the epithelium

questions.why: Answer: A.

notes.D: Vessels are in the lamina propria.

questions.stem: On circumvallate papillae, the taste buds lie on the:
questions.why: The free surface carries secondary papillae with thin smooth epithelium.

questions.stem: Enamel rods measure about:
questions.why: Enamel is about 2.5 mm thick.

questions.stem: The part of the tooth covered by enamel and visible above the gum line is the:
questions.why: The anatomical crown is all the enamel-covered part.

questions.stem: Dental caries begins when enamel is:
questions.why: Fluoride reduces caries.

questions.stem: The enamel organ is derived from:
questions.why: As a horseshoe-shaped band of oral epithelium.

questions.stem: The organic part of dentin is mainly:
questions.why: About 30% organic, from odontoblasts.

questions.stem: The outer edge of the dental pulp is formed by the:
questions.why: Their processes extend into the dentinal tubules.

questions.stem: Cementum differs from bone in that it:

options.label: A
options.text: has canaliculi that form no network

options.label: D
options.text: has no mineral content at all

questions.why: It is avascular and about 65% mineral.

questions.stem: Orthodontic tooth movement is possible because the:

options.label: B
options.text: tooth is fused directly to the bone

options.label: D
options.text: pulp regenerates new roots when needed

questions.why: Answer: A.

notes.B: Not so; a ligament joins them.

questions.stem: Saliva from the major glands is secreted mainly:

options.label: E
options.text: only when the mouth becomes dry

questions.why: Minor glands secrete continually.

questions.stem: Parasympathetic stimulation of the major salivary glands:
questions.why: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Serous secretion contains salivary amylase and:
questions.why: Mucous cells make mucin.

notes.D: Lingual lipase is from von Ebner's glands.

questions.stem: Compared with mucous acini, serous acini have:
questions.why: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Interlobular ducts of salivary glands are lined by:
questions.why: They join to form the main excretory duct.

questions.stem: Striated ducts are described as:

options.label: E
options.text: the site of HCO₃⁻ secretion only

questions.why: They are larger in serous glands.

questions.stem: At very high flow rates, the gland contributing most saliva is the:
questions.why: About 50% of stimulated saliva.

questions.stem: The parotid (Stensen's) duct opens opposite the:
questions.why: It crosses masseter and pierces buccinator.

questions.stem: The submandibular (Wharton's) duct emerges from the:
questions.why: It opens at the sublingual caruncle.

questions.stem: Bartholin's duct is associated with the:
questions.why: The larger sublingual duct, often joining the submandibular duct.

questions.stem: The submandibular gland lies within the:
questions.why: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which nerve is NOT closely related to the parotid gland?
questions.why: The lingual and hypoglossal nerves relate to the submandibular gland.

notes.E: Supplies it via the otic ganglion.

questions.stem: The parotid gland receives arterial supply from branches of the:
questions.why: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Mumps (parotitis) pain typically worsens:

options.label: A
options.text: when the gland secretes, e.g. at meals

options.label: B
options.text: when the patient is fast asleep

options.label: C
options.text: when the gland is fully at rest

options.label: D
options.text: when the patient lies down flat

options.label: E
options.text: in cold weather and at night

questions.why: The tight capsule is stretched by secretion.

questions.stem: The preferred surgical treatment for a ranula is:
questions.why: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Dry mouth (xerostomia) is a recognised feature of:
questions.why: Autoimmune destruction of salivary glands.

questions.stem: The skin over the angle of the mandible and the parotid is supplied by the:
questions.why: The rest of the face is supplied by CN V.
